Conclusion and evidence boundary

Observed problems include pale-surface white icons and overly dim gray text on dark panels. Pure black text on a dark surface was not stably reproduced in this live inspection. Most values and primary headings are clear; the weaker elements are parameter names, preset captions, explanatory text, and transport symbols on pale buttons.

User-reported black text on dark backgrounds: do not mark this exact failure as reproduced. The observed dark-panel issue is dim gray text. Explicit black foregrounds in the reviewed source are generally paired with bright surfaces. A separate capture-path comment documents near-black text in generated screenshots; investigate R02 without assuming it explains the live report.

Theme constraint: MediaWorkbenchApp.swift:22 forces .preferredColorScheme(.dark). Switching the OS to Light did not produce a complete light app theme. Pale button surfaces and controls were still inspected. The original system appearance was Auto and was restored.

Design targets, not certification

Use 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for necessary symbols as design targets. See W3C text contrast guidance and non-text contrast guidance. Disabled, decorative, and fully system-managed controls require applicability checks. This inspection does not establish complete accessibility compliance.

Contrast numbers are approximate raster estimates from current-run captures, converted to sRGB. Translucency, wallpaper tinting, antialiasing, and capture compression affect the samples. Resolve final foreground and background colors during implementation before making a compliance claim. Coordinates, representative colors, and methods are in contrast-samples.json.

P1 F01 · OBSERVED IN LIVE UI

White transport icons lose contrast against pale button surfaces

Video / Live Photo transport: previous frame, play, next frame, range zoom, and mute.

Observed behavior

Enabled circular controls have pale gray surfaces with white symbols. Representative screenshot colors are white on #D2D2D2, approximately 1.51:1. These are available controls, not the disabled Undo / Redo buttons.

Likely implementation cause

IconButton explicitly sets the symbol foreground to .primary. In the dark environment this resolves to a light foreground, while glassButton(.circle) produces a pale surface. The explicit label style appears to override the intended surface-aware foreground.

Recommended change

First test removing the explicit foreground override for ordinary symbols so the native button style can choose its foreground. If custom styling remains necessary, define foreground and button surface as a pair. Verify active accent symbols separately. Do not apply a global white foreground.

Acceptance criteria

  • Every enabled transport symbol is recognizable in normal, hover, pressed, and active states.
  • Target at least 3:1 for meaningful symbols against their actual button surfaces.
  • Check both system Light and Dark appearances and all IconButton call sites.
Reproduction and source locations
  • Open a video or Live Photo in the editor.
  • Inspect the available circular transport buttons below the preview in both system appearances.

P1 F02 · OBSERVED IN LIVE UI

Essential parameter and metadata labels are too dim on dark panels

Simple / Full Color, Geometry, Audio, and Info panels; parameter names, units, and metadata field names.

Observed behavior

Numeric values remain legible while the corresponding names become much darker. Approximate raster samples: parameter label 3.32:1; metadata field label 3.38:1. Meaningful units such as EV, degrees, and percent are even more subdued.

Likely implementation cause

ParameterRow uses .secondary whenever value == neutral. This visually conflates an unchanged, enabled parameter with an unavailable control. InfoPanel.row also uses .secondary, while the parameter suffix uses .tertiary.

Recommended change

Give essential labels a guaranteed readable foreground on the actual panel surface. Express modified / unmodified state through a marker, weight, or other treatment that preserves text contrast. Keep meaningful units readable. Avoid fixing only individual call sites when ParameterRow is the shared cause.

Acceptance criteria

  • Untouched enabled labels are readable before the user changes any value.
  • Check neutral, modified, and disabled states independently.
  • Target at least 4.5:1 for normal-size enabled text, including meaningful units.
Reproduction and source locations
  • Open a photo or video and expand basic adjustments.
  • Compare untouched parameter names with their numeric values.
  • Check Geometry position / angle controls, Audio volume, and Info metadata rows.

P2 F03 · OBSERVED IN LIVE UI

Available presets and unselected tabs look unavailable

Preset captions, Save Preset and Match Look entry points; inspector tabs, Simple / Full selector, and scope selector.

Observed behavior

The selected Original caption is clear; other available preset captions and entry points are much dimmer. The AI Look caption sample is approximately 3.34:1. Unselected segmented labels show a similar visual pattern, but each label was not individually measured.

Likely implementation cause

Preset captions use selected ? .primary : .secondary. GlassSegmentedControl also assigns Color.secondary to nonselected, nonhovered options. Available unselected and disabled appearances are insufficiently distinct.

Recommended change

Raise contrast for available unselected text. Use surface, stroke, or weight to distinguish the selected option. Reserve stronger dimming for genuinely disabled options. Keep the active, inactive-but-available, and disabled states distinct.

Acceptance criteria

  • All available preset names and tabs are readable without hover.
  • Selected options remain identifiable.
  • Measure normal-size enabled text against a 4.5:1 design target.
Reproduction and source locations
  • Open an ordinary photo and inspect the preset grid in Simple Color.
  • Compare the selected Original caption with other available preset captions.
  • Inspect available unselected inspector and scope tabs without hovering.

P2 F04 · OBSERVED IN LIVE UI

Learning groups, durations, and instructional hints are overly faint

Learn lesson list and the sample-photo hint in the first lesson step.

Observed behavior

Group headings and minute counts are difficult to read relative to lesson titles. Approximate samples: duration 2.28:1; sample-photo hint 2.33:1. The main lesson title and body are substantially clearer.

Likely implementation cause

Group headings, durations, and the sample-photo hint use .tertiary. InsightCard explanations also use .tertiary; that additional location was identified in source but not exhaustively expanded and reproduced in the live audit.

Recommended change

Keep explanatory text subordinate to titles without making it nearly disappear. Establish hierarchy through weight and spacing. Audit the related source-only InsightCard location during implementation.

Acceptance criteria

  • Lesson groups, durations, and instructional hints remain readable on dark surfaces.
  • Expand relevant learning explanations during regression testing.
  • Target at least 4.5:1 for normal-size informational text.

P2 F06 · OBSERVED IN LIVE UI

White text on light accent-filled controls has limited contrast

Export format / destination segments and primary actions; related lesson Next controls.

Observed behavior

Representative selected JPEG colors are white on #6A99CE, approximately 2.97:1 in the screenshot. This is a readability improvement item. Native system-drawn controls have applicability exceptions; this observation alone is not a formal WCAG failure determination.

Likely implementation cause

WorkbenchTheme.accent is derived from the system accent once at launch, and SheetContent applies it to native controls. The final visible surface is additionally affected by platform rendering.

Recommended change

Verify the accent surface and the foreground chosen by each control as a pair. Define onAccent for app-controlled surfaces. If retaining white text, ensure a sufficiently dark fill. Prefer native adaptation for system-managed controls and avoid blindly overriding their foregrounds.

Acceptance criteria

  • Inspect several system accents, selected segments, and primary buttons.
  • Target 4.5:1 for normal-size text where the app controls the color pair.
  • Evaluate native-control exceptions and actual platform behavior separately.
Reproduction and source locations
  • Open photo export with the current system accent.
  • Inspect the selected JPEG segment and primary action text.
  • Compare related accented controls in video export and the first lesson step.

Separate theme and capture-path items

R01 There is no complete light application theme to validate yet

The root view forces .preferredColorScheme(.dark). Panel and canvas colors, white opacity treatments, stars, and selection tokens are largely fixed for dark surfaces. System Light appearance does not create a full light application theme.

Implementation guardrail: Do not remove the forced dark scheme as an isolated fix. If full light-mode support is in scope later, define paired surface, text, selection, onSelection, accent, and onAccent tokens together. Removing the scheme alone could let semantic dark text appear on fixed dark surfaces.

R02 Near-black text may also occur in the snapshot capture path

The existing screenshot script documents that some window captures render secondary text on the translucent inspector as near-black. Its workaround renders the inspector separately and replaces the captured column. This comment is an investigation lead, not proof that the user-reported live issue is only a screenshot artifact.

Implementation guardrail: Compare the same state in a native window capture and DebugSnapshot output under system Light / Dark, active / inactive windows, and main / standalone panels. Do not treat replacing website screenshots as a fix for application contrast.

Instructions for the implementing AI

The user requested an audit report and will handle fixes later. This artifact does not itself authorize source edits or publication.

  • Read the referenced source and reproduce the current UI before changing behavior.
  • Keep this pass scoped to contrast and state clarity; preserve layout, copy, image processing, and data.
  • Prefer shared fixes and paired color roles over scattered literal white / black replacements.
  • Do not infer full light-theme support from system appearance switching.
  • Validate with fresh live captures and resolved colors; do not hide real UI issues with composited marketing screenshots.
  • Report confirmed fixes separately from source-only risks and remaining coverage gaps.

Suggested sequence

  1. F01: shared IconButton foreground / surface pairing
  2. F02 and F03: enabled label and tab contrast
  3. F04 and F05: informational text hierarchy
  4. F06 and R02: accent control review and capture-path comparison

Completion evidence to provide after authorized fixes

For each finding, report the code changes, the tested states, fresh live screenshots, resolved color measurements where available, and remaining exceptions. Keep source-only risks and loading-blocked surfaces separate from verified fixes.

Handoff files: index.html is the self-contained visual report. audit.json contains structured findings, reproduction steps, source locations, acceptance criteria, evidence IDs, coverage gaps, and guardrails. contrast-samples.json preserves the original approximate measurements.
